column1: # Rows db.pdbchain.* (line RG item K4j, 2026-11-17; tests/db_search/pdbchain/make_pdbchain.py): a version 4 database of five sequences without a title whose Seq-ids are gb|AB60000<n>.1| and a pdb Seq-id with a chain INTEGER (321, -191, 383, 65, none) and no chain-id: NCBI's x_SetTitleFromPDB makes the title `Chain A` from the low byte of the integer, isprint((unsigned char) m_PDBChain) (321, -191 and 65), none for 383 (0x7F) and an absent chain. The pdb Seq-id alone would not load for NCBI's report (`Unknown`, `no longer exists in database`), hence the gb one.

# Rows db.pdbchain.only.* (line RG-KB item 12, 2026-11-24; make_pdbchain.py `pdbonly`): the same records with the pdb Seq-id alone. NCBI's data loader looks up the Seq-id of the id's handle (the chain normalized to char(chain) read back as a signed char: 65 for 321 and -191, 127 for 383) and serves the sequence only where a stored id compares equal to it, so the records of chain 321, -191 and 383 have an empty Bioseq handle: outfmt 0 `Unknown` and `no longer exists in database...alignment skipped`, outfmt 1-4 leave their alignments out, XML `Unknown` with the catch's Hsp, XML2 and JSON the id alone, the tabular rows of a failed lookup, outfmt 18 no row; the default saccver is NCBI's null pointer exception (LOSAT's refusal).

# Rows db.pdbchain.norm.* (line RG-KB item 12 review 1, 2026-11-24; make_pdbchain.py `pdbnorm`): six records whose only Seq-id is a pdb one with a taxid: a lower-case molecule (chain 66, chain-id A), a release date that normalizes (month 13) and a chain of 200 without a chain-id have no Bioseq (the handle looks up chain 65, 65, -56); dates that do not normalize (month 16, a season) and a normalized chain equal to the stored one (65, chain-id A, month 13) load. The organism report shows the loaded ones with a taxonomy database (BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/good). NCBI's XML (outfmt 5) stops at the byte 0xC8 of chain 200's label (not UTF-8).

# Rows db.pdbchain.two.* (line RG-KB item 12 review 2, 2026-11-24; make_pdbchain.py `pdbtwo`): two records of two definition lines each, the first `pdb 1AB<n>` chain 321 without a chain-id (the Seq-align id; untitled for 1AB1, `t0` for 1AB2), the second `pdb|1AB<n>|A` titled `t1`, which holds the Seq-id of the handle: NCBI's data loader makes the reports' Bioseq of the second line (the description line, the organism report and the heading's generated title of the untitled line show `t1`; the heading lists both lines). Row db.pdbchain.norm.blastp.5q: `q_norm0.faa` (the letters of `1ab6`), whose first Hit is that of a subject without a Bioseq before NCBI's XML exception at `1AB8`.

# Rows db.pdbchain.seen.* (line RG-KB item 12, decision KB-12-1, 2026-11-25; make_pdbchain.py `q_pdb1ab1.faa`): the query pdb|1AB1|A read with -parse_deflines holds the id of the handle of `1AB1` chain 321 (chain 65), so NCBI's scope finds the query's Bioseq for that sequence (tabular.cpp:836-866): the tables show the query's ids, N/A for stitle and salltitles, the query record's length for slen and no taxonomy, the organism report the query's line without a taxid; the fields that read the found Bioseq's letters (sseq, and in BLASTP pident) and the other formats that read it keep LOSAT's refusal.
